name: Shaft
author: E. T. Carter
description: One to three fans of slanted volumetric light beams pour from chosen points around the frame and cross it diagonally — crepuscular rays in bunches, a few soft-edged shafts separated by dark gaps, each blooming and dying on its own slow phase while the fans rock a few degrees over about a minute, like moonlight bent through unseen water.

params.label: Swing
params.effect: Amplitude in degrees of the fan's slow rocking — 0 pins the beams perfectly still, 12 sweeps them noticeably across the frame.

params.label: Fade speed
params.effect: How quickly individual beams bloom in and fade out of the fan.

params.label: Beam width
params.effect: CSS-pixel width of a typical shaft — narrow gives many slivers of light, wide gives two or three broad columns.

params.label: Light sources
params.effect: How many points cast crepuscular fans — 1 a single corner shaft, 2 adds a mirrored fan from the opposite side, 3 adds a high overhead burst that lights the dark corners.

params.label: Source X
params.effect: Horizontal position of the primary light source as a fraction of frame width — negative sits it off the left edge, past 1 off the right.

params.label: Source Y
params.effect: Vertical position of the primary light source (1 is the top edge) — above 1 it sits off the top so the beams rake down into the frame.

params.label: Light intensity
params.effect: Overall brightness of the beams and haze — low gives faint moody shafts, high floods the frame with bright volumetric light.
